question: Can a mouse grow wings that actually support its flight?

generations.asked: a mouse with wings that can support its flight
a mouse with a patagium and a styliform cartilage that can support its flight
the generation-1 animal, entering flight from a 4 m drop instead of a jump
powered flight: wings that support the animal, not a membrane that slows its fall
the generation-1 animal with its three quantities declared, through the whole physics pipeline

chain.requirement: The designed mouse must carry a lifting surface on the forelimb whose area is large enough to support its body weight in flight, and this ladder must say which molecule, pathway, cell, cell-cell interaction, tissue and organ change would produce that surface.
chain.species_caveat: Only five links (l06, l08, l13, l14, l15) are mouse data, and every one of them is either ordinary trunk-skin thickening or a syndactyly defect; all patagium and wing evidence comes from a marsupial sugar glider, a rodent flying squirrel and bats, and none of it is data from a mouse that flies, because no such animal exists.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched in this run relates a membrane area to the body mass it can support. The physics layer's lifting_area_supports_mass: met used a DECLARED area; the one aerodynamic statement found (l18) is a narrative review sentence with no numbers, and the bat review that does discuss wing loading and wing area reports them only as postnatal growth curves for bats, never as a threshold a mouse-sized animal would have to clear.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A measured wing-area / body-mass (wing loading) dataset for small mammals, with a stated minimum area for a 20-30 g body, so the declared area could be checked rather than assumed.

missing_rungs.why: No mouse genotype in anything fetched produces a patagium or any membrane that spans a joint. The strongest mouse gain-of-function found (l08, inducible Wnt5a) thickens and densifies skin everywhere at once; the strongest mouse routes to webbing (l13, l14, l15) are syndactyly defects of the autopod. The gap between skin gets thicker, or digits stay fused, and a lifting surface exists is not crossed by any document fetched here.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A spatially restricted gain-of-function mouse - for example Wnt5a, or Fgf7 and Fgf10, driven in interlimb lateral dermis or in forelimb interdigital mesenchyme - scored for membrane outgrowth, area and span. This run found no record of such an experiment.

missing_rungs.why: In the bat, the species whose anatomy the design actually wants, the dermal-epidermal step cannot be tested: the authors state that reliance on field-collected embryos prevented in vivo or explant tests of WNT5A function. So the bat side of the ladder stops at association (l10) and never reaches necessity.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A bat embryo culture or electroporation system, or a captive breeding colony, allowing loss of function of Wnt5a or of the FGF7/FGF10 axis in the developing plagiopatagium.

missing_rungs.why: The flying squirrel fibroblast-to-keratinocyte interaction (l03) is a CellChat inference from single-nucleus transcriptomes, which the paper itself labels putative and candidate. Nothing fetched perturbs a receptor on the keratinocyte side in any gliding mammal.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Receptor-side perturbation, for example FGFR2 or a non-canonical WNT receptor, in patagium epidermis, with the dermal condensate and epidermal thickness scored.

missing_rungs.why: No document fetched gives any mechanical property of a retained interdigital web or of a patagium: no tensile strength, stiffness, thickness under load or failure point. A membrane that exists is not yet a membrane that bears a body.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Mechanical testing of patagium, and of retained interdigital webbing in the mouse syndactyly models above, against the aerodynamic load implied by the physics layer's 4 m drop.

missing_rungs.why: The ontology layer does not grant the designed organism the structure it needs, so the ladder cannot be named end to end. Querying Ubergraph in this run returned wing (UBERON_0000023) never_in_taxon Glires (NCBITaxon_314147) and never_in_taxon Metatheria (NCBITaxon_9263), while two of the three patagium papers fetched here describe gliding membranes in exactly those clades - a rodent flying squirrel and a marsupial sugar glider. patagium (UBERON_0010856) itself returned no never_in_taxon rows in this run. A mouse is Glires, so per the fetched axioms it is forbidden a wing.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Either an Uberon revision removing or narrowing the wing never_in_taxon Glires and Metatheria axioms, or a decision in this project to land the mouse ladder on patagium rather than wing.

missing_rungs.why: Found by adversarial verification, not declared by the builder. The pathway -> cell rung is occupied by exactly one link, l02, and l02 does not cross it. Its quote reports only that two fibroblast subpopulations (Fp2, Fr) are patagium-enriched by differential abundance and expression; the link's own what_it_does_not_show concedes 'nothing here shows the WNT pathway is required to produce them'. Pathway and cell are joined only by appearing in the same snRNA-seq dataset, while the link's relation field claims specifies_fate, which the quote does not support. Two further links, l05 and l12, route pathway -> cell_cell straight past the cell rung with skipped_rung left null, which is the same gap showing up as undeclared bookkeeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A perturbation of non-canonical WNT (ligand or receptor) in gliding-mammal patagium dermis, or in mouse lateral dermis, scored for whether the Fp2/Fr fibroblast states form - i.e. an experiment making the pathway responsible for the cell identity, rather than co-detected with it.

verification.method: Python string matching, not reading by eye: every quote and every source document was normalised identically (HTML entities unescaped, XML tags replaced by a space, Unicode dashes and curly quotes folded to ASCII, NBSP folded, all whitespace runs collapsed to one space) and the quote was required to occur as an exact substring of the normalised document. Failures would have been diagnosed by binary-searching the longest matching prefix and by re-searching every other file in the raw directory.

quotes.note: All 19 quotes occur byte-for-byte in the file named in quote_from, under whitespace and XML-tag-boundary normalisation only. No quote was paraphrased, stitched from two places or attributed to the wrong file.

fetch_log.note: Each of the 9 distinct quote_from files resolves to a call in runs/_chains/log/flying-mouse.fetch.json with status 200 and a matching saved_to path. The two documents that failed (PMC1622783, PMC2579364 full text, HTTP 500) are not used as quote_from sources; their abstracts, fetched 200 from NCBI efetch, are, and refused_sources already records the failure and what it cost.

upheld_after_challenge.why: Challenged: the quote hedges ('raised the possibility') and the fetched text names neither species nor cell line for the scratch assay. Upheld because adding recombinant FGF7/FGF10 and measuring a significant increase in migration is a gain of function that changes the process, which is the brief's sufficiency. The caveat stands that the assay involves no identified keratinocytes, no fibroblasts and no patagium, so it does not support the cell_cell entity this link names.

FGF7/FGF10-soaked beads implanted in mouse skin explant, epidermal thickness increased versus PBS: gain of function, correctly graded. Note the relation field says required_for, which is the opposite of what a bead-addition experiment shows; the same relation/grade mismatch appears on l07 and l08.
Doxycycline-inducible Wnt5a double-transgenic with histology and KRT14 IHC: gain of function, correctly graded.
Nog null mouse with failure of webbing regression: loss of function, correctly graded.
Conditional Akirin2 knockout in limb epithelium retaining the interdigital web: loss of function, correctly graded.

Ectopic interdigital Shh from an enhancer-adopting insertion, with CRISPR deletions and a reporter, producing webbing: gain of function, correctly graded, and conservatively so given the reporter and epistasis evidence in that paper.
A comparative growth-rate statement in a review is a correlation, which is what association means, so unlike l18 it was left alone.

walkability.longest_entity_continuous_walk: l01 -> l02 -> l03 -> l07 -> l09 -> l10 spans all seven levels with each link's to-entity matching the next link's from-entity, so the ladder is nominally complete. It is not a walk: it changes species twice (flying squirrel for l01-l03, sugar glider for l07 and l09, bat for l10), every link in it is association except l07, and it terminates at a bat plagiopatagium rather than at any lifting surface on a mouse. No species-continuous walk from molecule to phenotype exists in this ladder, and none exists in a mouse at all.

walkability.honest_gaps_left_untouched: All six breaks the builder declared were re-read and none was softened or removed: organ->phenotype, molecule->organ, cell_cell->tissue, cell->cell_cell, tissue->organ and the molecule->pathway ontology obstruction (wing never_in_taxon Glires) all stand as written.
